heading: Names are whole English words
body:
A reader should understand a name without guessing, even when English is not their first language. So Tachyon splits every class, method, field and parameter name into words, at capital letters, `_`, `-` and digits: `calcTotal` is `calc` and `total`, and `order_id` is `order` and `id`. Each word must be one of these:

- a word in the English word list that `ty` ships (American and British spellings, with their endings, such as `orders`, `created` or `colour`);
- a short technical word: `id`, `url`, `uri`, `html`, `css`, `json`, `api`, `http`, `https`, `ui`, `db`, `sql`, `jwt`, `uuid`, `io`, `os`, `xml`, `csv`, `pdf`, `svg`, `config`, `utils`, `async`, `sku` and a few more;
- a word of your domain that you list: `tac.names.words` in `client/manifest.json` for Tac and `names.words` in `server/application.json` for Yon, such as `["fylo"]` for a product name;
- two English words written as one, such as `username` or `webhook`.

A clipped word is refused even when a dictionary knows it, and the help gives the whole word:

| Write | Not |
| --- | --- |
| `user` | `usr` |
| `config` | `cfg` |
| `calculate` | `calc` |
| `total` | `tot` |
| `button` | `btn` |
| `message` | `msg` |
| `context` | `ctx` |
| `request`, `response` | `req`, `res` |
| `index` | `idx` |
| `error` | `err` |
| `temporary` | `tmp` |
| `value` | `val` |
| `number` | `num` |
| `text` | `str` |
| `documents` | `docs` |

Local variables are not checked, and neither are names that the language or a base type chooses for you: constructors, Python `__init__`, methods marked `override`, and the methods of `impl Trait for Type` in Rust.

The build refuses a name with `TY1328`, for example: The parameter name `itemIdx` in CartService is not plain English: `idx` is short for `index`. Rename it to `itemIndex`.

One trap in Tac: do not name a service field after the instance name of another service. A field `documentation` next to a `DocumentationService` is read as that service, not as a property. Pick another word, such as `documents`.

This check is new, so you can turn it off for one side of the app while you move code. For Tac code, set `tac.names.check` to `false` in `client/manifest.json`. For Yon code, set `names.check` to `false` in `server/application.json`. Use these settings only for migration. `ty migrate check` lists every place to change, even when the setting is off.
